title: The hippocampus as a latent diffusion engine for memory, perception and cognitive dysfunction
title_zh: 作为记忆、感知和认知功能障碍潜在扩散引擎的海马体
abstract: Abstract The hippocampus is a central cognitive hub whose dysfunction contributes to most neurodegenerative dementias. Despite extensive knowledge of its anatomy, physiology and circuitry, a unifying account that links hippocampal dynamics to cognition and clinical syndromes remains lacking. Drawing on systems neuroscience and recent advances in generative artificial intelligence, we conceptualize the hippocampus as a latent diffusion engine that compresses sensory, interoceptive and cognitive inputs into low-dimensional representations and regenerates percepts, episodic memories and imagined scenes for cortical integration. Travelling waves of cortico-hippocampal oscillations, aligned with large-scale functional gradients, schedule and structure this generative process and organize distributed neural activity into coherent, semantically grounded constructs. We formalize this proposal as stochastic latent oscillatory diffusion (SLOD), a biologically grounded framework that maps hippocampal-cortical computations onto specific anatomical substrates and dynamical processes. While we do not suggest that the hippocampus implements diffusion algorithms per se, we show that its computations can be decomposed into homologous operations including compression, stochastic exploration, conditioning and reconstruction, whose formal structure closely parallels that of latent diffusion models. Finally, we demonstrate how major neurodegenerative dementias, including the Alzheimer’s disease spectrum, dementia with Lewy bodies and frontotemporal dementia, can be understood as selective breakdowns of distinct components of this generative architecture.
abstract_zh: 摘要 海马体是一个核心的认知枢纽，其功能障碍与大多数神经退行性痴呆症有关。尽管对其解剖学、生理学和电路有深入了解，但将海马体动力学与认知及临床综合征相关联的统一理论仍然缺乏。借鉴系统神经科学和生成式人工智能的最新进展，我们将海马体概念化为一种潜在扩散引擎，它将感觉、内感受和认知输入压缩为低维表示，并再生感知、情景记忆和想象场景以供皮层整合。与大尺度功能梯度对齐的皮层-海马体振荡传播波调度并结构化这一生成过程，并将分布的神经活动组织成具有语义基础的连贯结构。我们将这一提议形式化为随机潜在振荡扩散（SLOD），这是一个基于生物学的框架，将海马-皮层计算映射到特定的解剖基质和动态过程上。尽管我们并不认为海马体本身实现扩散算法，但我们表明其计算可以分解为压缩、随机探索、条件化和重建等同源操作，其形式结构与潜在扩散模型密切相关。最后，我们展示了如何理解阿尔茨海默病谱系、路易体痴呆和额颞叶痴呆等主要神经退行性痴呆症，将其视为这种生成架构不同组成部分的选择性崩溃。
